thread:
Emma (Head of Product): thanks for joining the live Q&A. wanted to capture the takeaways about why were winning vs losing and list follow-ups. i'll keep it tight.
Ivy (Sales): quick signals from pipeline: wins = stable p95, transparent pricing, and pilot docs. losses = no HSM option, unpredictable latency under burst, and vague answers about model drift.
Sophia (CS): one concrete loss: DataStream switched after a hallucination in a critical billing flow. they needed reproducible evals and an SLA for model behavior during deploys.
Ben (Customer Success): recurring asks we hear: 1) "one-week private/VPC path" 2) "latency tiers + pricing" 3) "eval kit + playbook for regressions" 4) "clear escalation path with response times".
Lin (Eng PM): engineering view: short-term (2-3 sprints) = VPC quickstart docs + terraform module, CI release-check script for quantization toggles, and a simple fallback routing policy. long-term = HSM on-prem connector and SLA-grade dedicated capacity.
Omar (Security): on HSM ask  we can offer a managed KMS + bring-your-own-HSM workflow, but it needs legal review and SOC evidence. estimate: 3-4 months for a secure, auditable path.
Maria (Applied ML): model quality root cause: some customers saw regression after we flipped a default quant profile. mitigation: add a sampled eval check in CI and surface top-10 prompt regressions in the console. low-effort and high impact.
Ivy (Sales): question for leadership: can we offer a paid "latency guarantee" tier? a couple of banks want contractual p95. they'd pay significantly.
David (CEO): yes, we should explore a premium latency tier. product + finance to propose pricing and expected cost. include fallback behavior so we don't take unbounded risk.
Emma (Head of Product): proposal for owners: Lin = VPC quickstart one-pager (scope + beta definition), Maria = quantization/regression FAQ + small CI harness, Ben + Ivy + Lin = "why-we-lost" playbook draft, Omar = security checklist for HSM.
allhands-bot: :spiral_calendar: tasks created: "VPC quickstart one-pager" owner: Lin, due: 7 days; "loss-playbook" owner: Ben, due: 2 weeks.
Sophia (CS): small ask: include cost delta examples for batching vs latency in the FAQ. customers want numbers not just theory.
Maria (Applied ML): will include sample token-cost deltas and a tiny table of expected accuracy shifts per quant profile.
Lin (Eng PM): i'll scope the 2-3 sprint plan for the quickstart and call out the limited beta constraints (X customers, telemetry on, support level). will post the one-pager here.
David (CEO): leadership will review the one-pagers and commitments next Wed. please make them concise and list risks + mitigation.
Emma (Head of Product): thanks everyone  i'll convert these into tickets after the review. please keep further replies short so i can synthesize. :thumbsup:
